expectation: I expect the hydrogen supply to be positioned at the reactor, ready for a further step; this alone may not start the reaction.

effect: The hydrogen is positioned at the reactor, and the carbon dioxide can now be combined with it there.
reaction: The preparation worked as expected; I’m curious about the reactor’s output.
reason: Combining the two inputs at the reactor directly advances the goal of making fuel.

effect: The reactor is collecting methane, and the condensed reaction water now needs a return path.
reaction: Seeing some of the well’s hydrogen return as water makes the loop clearer.
reason: The hose is the only available combination and should connect the cooled water return.

effect: The hose connects the reactor’s water return to treatment and electrolysis, completing the loop and reducing the need for new water.
reaction: It was satisfying to see how the reaction water can be used again.

mostWorthwhile.text: Starting the reactor was most worthwhile: the methane and condensed water made the connection between the inputs and the water loop concrete.

leastWorthwhile.text: Placing the hydrogen was a straightforward preparation with little to discover on its own.

surprise.text: The explanation that some hydrogen from the well becomes water again made the loop clearer.

arbitrary.text: No action felt purposeless, though choosing which reactor input to place first seemed arbitrary.

continue.text: Yes. I would want to see what happens to the specimens and the early return, and whether the fuel plant is enough to get them home.
